cleared.check: Part one of L-655: every unexecuted range and every one-sided or never-taken JUMPI of the 24,009 byte build, mapped to its source construct through the solc 0.8.26 source map of a rebuild with the settings of compile.js (runtime byte-identical to build/PoolManager.json).
cleared.result: Before set 6: 9,959 of 10,418 instructions, 255 JUMPI both ways, 129 one way, 3 never. Of the 132, 51 were ABI decoder or callvalue guards (jump to revert(0,0) at pc 816), 9 lock checks (ManagerLocked), 7 Panic 0x41, 3 Panic 0x11, 2 Panic 0x12, 7 SafeCast reverts, and the rest hook paths, ERC-6909 allowance paths, clear, settle with value, delegatecall guard, bounds checks and large-number branches of SqrtPriceMath and FullMath. cleared.check: Part two of L-655: pmdiff6.py, 706 scripts and 25,681 calls in the reference interpreter (pyevm.py) on the build, with a driver that can send value, delegatecall, staticcall, run outside unlock and return malformed callback data, hook doubles for every permission bit and return-delta combination, hook self-calls, a token whose balanceOf reverts or returns short data, failing native payouts with revert data of 0 to 1000 bytes, bounds of initialize, modifyLiquidity and swap, the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp, the 512 bit branch of mulDiv by 2^128 in Position.update, protocol fee collection while synced, and truncated calldata for every function.
cleared.result: Coverage of the six sets together: 10,288 of 10,418 instructions (98.75 percent, up from 95.6), 338 JUMPI both ways, 46 one way, 3 never. 83 of the 132 jumps now go both ways. jumpmap-after.json gives each remaining one with what it decides and why its other side is unreachable: 39 decide a revert, 9 a payout or price and 1 a credit, and none of the 49 can be reached by an ordinary caller in a transaction that pays out.

cleared.check: pmdiff6 on all 21 endpoints by eth_call with state override, each record compared with the reference interpreter (705 scripts; one is too long for the reference).
cleared.result: Per network, scripts equal to the reference: 1 703/705; 10 705/705; 8453 705/705; 130 703/705; 7777777 703/705; 480 705/705; 57073 703/705; 1868 703/705; 42220 703/705; 196 703/705; 42161 703/705; 4663 703/705; 99901 703/705; 137 700/705; 56 704/705; 43114 703/705; 143 703/705; 4326 703/705; 4217 703/705; 5042 701/705; 999 701/705. Every difference falls into one of three groups. (a) Four scripts in which a swap at tick spacing 1 walks the whole price range (8.1 to 14.9 million reference instructions): the first differing call is that swap failing with empty return data on the endpoint with less gas, and on 279 the whole record is empty (all networks except OP Mainnet, Base and World Chain for 277 and 279; Polygon, Arc and HyperEVM also for 275 and 276). (b) Script 682: take(currency 0x1000) succeeds in the reference because 0x1000 has no code there, and reverts with WrappedError(ERC20TransferFailed) on Polygon and BNB Smart Chain, where 0x1000 holds a system contract (eth_getCode returned 14,347 and 29,871 bytes), and on Monad. (c) Scripts 681 and 682 on Monad return nothing: 0x1000 is the staking precompile there, which reverts with 'method not supported' and consumes all gas given to it, so after about three such calls the script runs out of gas. Every other record, including all hook, ERC-6909, clear, settle, fallback and fee-growth paths, is byte-identical on all 21 networks.

cleared.check: Monad staking precompile at 0x1000 consumes all gas on a failing call, met through sync(0x1000) and take(0x1000) in pmdiff6.
cleared.result: An eth_call of three sync(0x1000) calls returns nothing while one or two return the full record, and eth_estimateGas of one call is 22,596,024. Monad documents that calls with invalid arguments consume all gas and that STATICCALL reverts (https://docs.monad.xyz/reference/staking/api, https://docs.monad.xyz/reference/staking/overview). The PoolManager reaches 0x1000 only as a currency or recipient the caller names, so the gas loss falls on the caller of its own pool. Earlier cycles already cleared 0x1000 as a currency and hook on Monad.

cleared.check: System contracts at 0x1000 on Polygon and BNB Smart Chain revert transfer(address,uint256) called by the PoolManager.
cleared.result: take of that currency reverts with ERC20TransferFailed (pmdiff6 script 682). This only makes a caller-chosen currency unusable; no pool of real tokens uses it. Polygon's native face at 0x1010 is F-008 and F-077.

cleared.check: Credit-deciding jumps that went one way in the first five sets: clear of an exact positive delta (PoolManager.sol:314-318), the infinite and finite allowance paths of transferFrom and burn (ERC6909.sol:155-158, ERC6909Claims.sol:224-229), afterSwap, afterAddLiquidity and afterRemoveLiquidity without the return-delta flag (Hooks.sol:163, 220-243, 298-302), the hook-as-caller returns (Hooks.sol:172, 217, 253, 293), native settle and settleFor with value (PoolManager.sol:349-365), and the 512 bit branch of mulDiv by 2^128 in Position.update (Position.sol:263-268).
cleared.result: All now go both ways in the reference and the results match the source: clear of the exact delta zeroes it and unlock completes, a finite allowance drops by the amount moved and an infinite one does not, a hook without the return-delta flag gets a zero delta, a hook calling the PoolManager itself skips its own callbacks and deltas, and the 512 bit fee branch always ends in SafeCastOverflow at Pool.sol:192 because the fee is then at least 2^128. The answers are byte-identical on all 21 networks.

cleared.check: The overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp (SqrtPriceMath.sol:42-52), taken by no earlier script.
cleared.result: A swap step stops short of its target only while the input left is below what the target needs, and each position's deposit is capped below 2^127 by toInt128 (Pool.sol:212-235). For amount times price to pass 2^256, the step must start below price 2^96 and run toward the bottom of the range, which needs an input above 2^160. pmdiff6 reaches the fallback that way, including the window where numerator1 plus the product wraps, and the swap then always reverts with SafeCastOverflow at Pool.sol:455-459. So the fallback never sets a price that is paid out. The same bound makes the amount > 2^160 branch of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount1RoundingDown (SqrtPriceMath.sol:102-106, pc 20776 and the never-reached 20942, 20963, 20971) need about 2^33 deposits.

cleared.check: Dead or redundant branches left one-sided: SELFBALANCE in Currency.balanceOfSelf (pc 15021), second success tests after the unlockCallback CALL and the balanceOf STATICCALL (pc 9048, 15094), and bytes4(data) of a hook call shorter than 4 bytes (pc 16370).
cleared.result: balanceOfSelf is only called for a nonzero currency (PoolManager.sol:281-285 and 353-359), so its native branch cannot run. The two success tests repeat a test that already left on failure (pc 9042, 15088), and hook calldata always comes from abi.encodeCall. None of them can be steered by a network that executes the earlier test correctly, and that earlier test is covered both ways on all 21 networks.

Every one-sided jump left in the build maps to a guard that the bounds above make unreachable, so no credit decision in the bytecode stays untested on the 21 networks.

leadResults.answer: pmdiff6.py (706 scripts) brings the build to 10,288 of 10,418 instructions and 338 of 387 conditional jumps taken both ways. Of the 132 jumps that were one way or never, 83 now go both ways. The other 49 are guards made unreachable by bounds in the source, or dead code, and jumpmap-after.json gives the reason for each. On all 21 endpoints every record equals the reference except four scripts where a swap across the whole range ran out of gas, and scripts that call address 0x1000, which holds a system contract on Polygon and BNB Smart Chain and the staking precompile on Monad. No credit-deciding jump is one-sided in a way a network could exploit.
